<div class="tag">Model types</div>

## What goes in, what comes out.<br><span class="then">Three common shapes of model.</span>

<div class="nn-types">
  <div class="nn-type">
    <div class="nn-io">
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:wave}}<span>audio</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end model">{{ICON:model}}<span>model</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:wave}}<span>audio</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="card-title">Audio to audio</div>
    <div class="nn-examples"><span>Examples:</span> RAVE, Demucs, amp models</div>
  </div>
  <div class="nn-type">
    <div class="nn-io">
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:sliders}}<span>parameters</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end model">{{ICON:model}}<span>model</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:wave}}<span>audio</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="card-title">Parameters to audio</div>
    <div class="nn-examples"><span>Examples:</span> DDSP, text-to-speech</div>
  </div>
  <div class="nn-type">
    <div class="nn-io">
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:wave}}<span>audio</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end model">{{ICON:model}}<span>model</span></div>
      <div class="nn-arrow">→</div>
      <div class="nn-end">{{ICON:sliders}}<span>parameters</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="card-title">Audio to parameters</div>
    <div class="nn-examples"><span>Examples:</span> PESTO, CREPE, speech-to-text</div>
  </div>
</div>

Note:
    - Audio → audio: runs every block at audio rate, the model is the effect; its latency is the plugin's latency.
    - Parameters → audio: control rate in, audio out, the model is the sound generator; has to deliver every block.
    - Audio → parameters: the model listens; the result often leaves the audio thread (UI, MIDI, file).

Note:
    - Stateless: output depends only on this call's input; context has to come with the input (overlapping windows); calls are independent.
    - Stateful: memory from one call to the next (RNN hidden states, cached convolution history); calls in order, one state per stream, reset when the stream restarts.

Note:
    - Conditioned: the controls are inputs too, and have to reach the model at the right time.
    - Causal: a model that looks ahead needs future samples, so its output is late by that much.
    - Fixed input size: the host block size rarely matches; step 2 is about this.
    - Rates: not everything runs per sample; control and note rates change how often the model is called.

  <div class="vae-meta">Realtime Audio Variational autoEncoder · stateful</div>
</div>

Note:
    - Real activations: a 220 Hz sine, block 6, run through the ONNX export (scripts/render_model_figure.py). Ink = positive, lilac = negative, each map scaled to its own maximum.
    - PQMF splits the block into 16 bands of 128 steps. Each strided convolution then trades time for channels: 192 x 32, 384 x 8, 768 x 2, 1536 x 1. The values do not shrink until the last step: 1536 numbers become the latent.
    - The latent is 128-dimensional, PCA-rotated; the export keeps the first 8 (fidelity 0.9). The file name says z16, the model card says 16 latent dimensions; encode() returns 8.
    - The decoder mirrors it with transposed convolutions, then the inverse PQMF merges the 16 bands back into 2048 samples.

<div class="tag">Training data</div>

## Trained on a magnetic resonator piano.<br><span class="then">Electromagnets play its strings.</span>

<div class="mrp">
  <figure><img src="assets/images/mrp/piano.jpg" alt="A grand piano fitted with the magnetic resonator piano kit"></figure>
  <figure><img src="assets/images/mrp/magnets.jpg" alt="The electromagnets above the strings, with their wiring"></figure>
</div>

<div class="mrp-caption">Recorded for <em>Strengjavera</em> (Jack Armitage, AIMC 2023), where artificial life plays the piano · model: Intelligent Instruments Lab, CC BY-NC 4.0 · photos: Aurelien Guichard, CC BY-SA 2.0</div>

Note:
    - The magnetic resonator piano (Andrew McPherson, 2009): an electromagnet above each string, so a grand piano can sustain endlessly, swell from silence and bend pitch, without loudspeakers.
    - Strengjavera ("string being"): an installation in which artificial life programs (Tölvera) drive the MRP. The model was trained on its sound; the model card does not give the length of the recordings.
    - Model: huggingface.co/Intelligent-Instruments-Lab/rave-models, mrp_strengjavera_b2048_r44100_z16.ts. Paper: aimc2023.pubpub.org/pub/83k6upv8 (CC BY 4.0).
    - Photos: commons.wikimedia.org, "Magnetic Resonator Piano" and "... details 1", Aurelien Guichard, CC BY-SA 2.0, resized.
